newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian oil price decision said unlikely this week.
newsitem.headline: Indian oil price decision said unlikely this week.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition is not likely to decide at a meeting this week whether to raise oil prices to plug a mounting subsidy bill, a government official said on Tuesday.
"I doubt that they will decide on Friday," said the official, who asked not to be identified. Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party coalition is scheduled to meet on Friday in the capital.
Petroleum Minister Janeshwar Mishra said on Monday the ruling centre-left coalition might have to postpone this week's meeting because he could not attend.

The government official said the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee was still expected to meet on Friday, but would probably not take up the oil price issue as Mishra would be out of town attending a party meeting.
He said the ruling alliance intended to take a final decision on oil prices before parliament reconvenes for a month-long monsoon session on July 23.
The government owes state oil companies an estimated 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) and the companies have complained they cannot keep importing crude unless domestic prices are raised.
